newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to earn 20 bln dmk via privatisation-paper.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to earn 20 bln dmk via privatisation-paper.

text.p: The German government plans to earn over 20 billion marks in the next 18 months by selling off real estate and stepping up privatisation, mass circulation daily Bild reported on Tuesday.
The money would be earned in 1997 and 1998, the newspaper said, providing a breakdown of where the funds would come from.
Citing a confidential Finance Ministry document, Bild Zeitung said the Bonn government plans to earn 3.1 billion marks by privatising postal bank Post Bank this year.
Additionally the government plans to earn 1.4 billion marks through further privatistation of German airline Deutsche Lufthansa this year.

Next year some 10 billion marks would be earned by selling off a further stake in telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG, while one billion marks would be earned from the final step in privatising Lufthansa.
The government also plans to sell government owned apartments and motorway restaurants.
The Finance Ministry was not immediately available for comment.
Bonn has been scrambling to find new funds in order paper of budget papers in time to qualify for entry into Europe's planned currency union, scheduled to begin in 1999.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel had already announced plans to step up privatisation and efforts to sell off more Telekom shares, but he had not given specific details.
